all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The new Bank Act allows chartered banks to make conventional mortgage loans on both residential and industrial construction, increasing their ability to compete for deposits and potentially increasing the availability of mortgage funds.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing the availability of mortgage funds, the reform aims to stimulate residential construction and address the growing housing needs.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The new Bank Act has been in effect since last May.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant change in the banking sector's role in mortgage financing, potentially stabilizing the housing market and addressing housing shortages.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The new Bank Act, in effect since last May, permits chartered banks to make conventional mortgage loans on both residential and industrial construction up to 75 per cent of the value of the property.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on mortgage loans for residential and industrial construction, which does not relate to R&D funding or innovation instruments for firms.
